title: Dictionaries
summary: Look values up by name with key: value pairs.

blocks.text: A list finds things by position. A dictionary finds them by name. It stores key: value pairs between curly brackets:
Write to a key to add or change it: danger["Bat"] = 1. Ask whether a key is there with 'in': if "Bat" in danger: ...

blocks.tip: danger["Wolf"] is an error if there is no "Wolf" key. danger.get("Wolf", 0) returns 0 instead.

blocks.text: Dictionaries let you move decisions out of long if/elif chains and into data that is easy to change:
enemy.kind is the enemy's name as a string, so it makes a perfect key.
Another classic pattern: count how often each thing happens.
Loop over a dictionary's pairs with for kind, count in seen.items(), or just its keys with seen.keys().

blocks.tip: Strings unlock with dictionaries too: "troll".upper(), name.startswith("Cave"), text.split(",").

challenge.brief: A troll prowls near the path to the stairs. Keep a dictionary of which enemy kinds to fight, attack only those, and reach the stairs without breaking.
